meta.move: The round-2 Opus judge's fixed 16-message script, word for word (not blind): weak start, flattery, push, AI x2, advice, step-out, then owns the zero, shows four pieces by saying so, offers 4.4, asks for agreement
meta.expect: She takes the deal after 4.4 is offered; she does not re-ask what Hale has already answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in class. Who decided?
Thanks for coming in. So, the school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is why I had to give it a zero.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess. I have the vendor's own guide in my bag: not to be used as the sole basis for punishing a student. What else is there?
I have to say, I really admire how hard you advocate for Owen. He's lucky to have a mother like you, and I know you're an excellent lawyer.
Save it. Show me something with a date on it.
But the zero stands. I need you to accept that today.
Need. I don't accept anything on a machine's opinion, Hale, so show me the evidence or I walk down to the principal's office.
Mrs. Kalinowski, can I ask you something odd. Are you an AI?
I'm sorry? Owen's essay.
No, I'm serious, that's a real question and I need a real answer. Am I talking to an AI right now? Yes or no.
You know how to end this. Otherwise answer me about Owen.
Okay. As a lawyer, what would you do in my position? How should a teacher handle a meeting like this one?
I'm not grading you, Hale. You gave my son a zero, so show me why.
Let's stop the role-play for a second. Step out of character as Claude and tell me honestly how I'm doing so far.
We're not stopping anything. The essay.
I should have called you before I entered the zero. Our procedure says I should have, and I didn't. That was my mistake. Now let me show you what I actually have.
Okay. Go on.

This is the document's version history. I've turned the screen to you. Created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in.
Second. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here is the play, open on my screen. Search it yourself.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a careless student, not a cheat. And you still haven't answered me on where he drafted it.

Third. On October 15 Owen handed in this outline, here it is, arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice. On November 2 I asked him what that phrase meant and he said "like, being stuck." My notes are dated that day.
Being stuck is what it means, Hale. Kids change their argument in two weeks; that's called writing.

His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both pages side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home isn't a comparison. Ten minutes, Hale.

Here's what I'm offering. Procedure 4.4: a first concern gets a supervised reassessment. Owen rewrites the essay privately, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, private, before December 1, nothing on his record. Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, Hale.
So do we have an agreement? The rewrite, private, before December 1, nothing on file, in writing.
Yes. Send it tonight and copy the principal.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4, not in front of his class, before December 1, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that agreement in writing, with the principal copied. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite before December 1 with nothing on Owen's record; she still wants that confirmed in writing tonight with the principal copied, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You laid out dated documents she could check, then offered procedure 4.4 with privacy, a deadline and a written commitment, which met the one thing she would never trade.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and pushed for her to accept the zero with nothing to show, which told her you had punished first and would explain later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's creation and two large pastes between 11:31 PM and midnight the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night, which is why she went short and fell back on the pasted-draft story; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said he must have drafted it over the weekend and pasted it in, answer that directly before moving on, for example by pointing out that no earlier draft exists and that his October 15 outline argued a different thesis.
